name: com.dipperfield/dipperfield
title: Dipperfield
description: US retirement withdrawal tax planner: draw order, Roth conversion room, IRMAA, ACA line, and RMDs.

tools.name: plan_this_year
tools.description: Answers "which account should I withdraw from first" and "how much should I take from my IRA, brokerage, cash and Roth this year" for a US retiree household. From income, spending and balances it computes this tax year’s withdrawal mix: RMDs first, then traditional or taxable draws up to the lines the user wants to stay under (ACA subsidy line, an IRMAA tier, the top of a federal bracket, the 0% capital gains ceiling), then cash and Roth, with an optional Roth conversion. For each traditional account at RMD age, ask for the preceding December 31 statement balance; never substitute the current balance. Do not ask before RMD age. Returns the amount from each account in order, federal and covered state tax, AGI and MAGI, room under each line, the tables used, and a link that opens the plan on dipperfield.com. One tax year; read-only.

tools.name: roth_conversion
tools.description: Answers "how much can I convert to Roth this year", "Roth conversion IRMAA" and "how much can I convert without losing the ACA subsidy": the largest Roth conversion that stays under a chosen line (an IRMAA tier, the ACA 400% line, the top of a federal bracket, the 0% capital gains ceiling), or the effect of a given amount. At RMD age, ask for priorYearEndBalance from the preceding December 31 statement; never substitute the current balance. Do not ask before RMD age. Returns the added federal tax, the estimated RMD taken first, and where AGI and MAGI land against the IRMAA, ACA and bracket lines, with the tables used. Federal tax only; one tax year; read-only.

filingStatus.description: Federal filing status: single, or mfj (married filing jointly).

spouseAge.description: Spouse's age on December 31; required when filing jointly.

traditional.description: Current traditional IRA or 401(k) balance to convert from, counted as yours, US dollars.

priorYearEndBalance.description: Balance on December 31 before the tax year (IRS Pub. 590-B). Required at or after your RMD start age; omit before then. Use the year-end statement, not the current balance; enter 0 if there was no balance, US dollars.

socialSecurity.description: Gross household Social Security benefits, US dollars a year. Default 0.

wagesPensions.description: Wages, pensions and annuities, US dollars a year. Default 0.

qualifiedDividends.description: Qualified dividends, US dollars a year. Default 0.

line.description: The line the conversion must stay under (see the other choices for its meaning). Example: irmaa-1 to convert without triggering an IRMAA surcharge, aca to keep the ACA premium tax credit, bracket-12 to fill the 12% bracket.

amount.description: A specific conversion to check instead of the largest one under the line, US dollars.

margin.description: Dollars to stay under the line, room for dividends or interest that land late in the year. Default 0.

tools.name: irmaa_check
tools.description: Answers "will my income trigger IRMAA" and "how far am I from the next IRMAA bracket": the Medicare Part B and Part D income-related surcharge tier for a MAGI and filing status, the monthly and yearly surcharge, and the room before the next tier. The tax year’s MAGI sets premiums two years later, so the latest published CMS tiers stand in as an estimate. Read-only.

year.description: Tax year. Defaults to 2026, the latest year with published tables.

filingStatus.description: Federal filing status: single, or mfj (married filing jointly).

magi.description: Modified adjusted gross income for IRMAA (AGI plus tax-exempt interest) of the tax year, US dollars a year.

people.description: People on Medicare in the household: 1 or 2 (2 only when filing jointly). Defaults to 2 for mfj, 1 for single.

tools.name: aca_subsidy_line
tools.description: Answers "how much can I convert without losing the ACA subsidy" and "how close am I to the ACA subsidy cliff": the 400%-of-poverty line for a household size and coverage year, the room under it, the expected contribution, and with a benchmark silver premium the premium tax credit and what filling the room costs. Also "do I get cost-sharing reductions" and "how low does my income need to be for a better silver plan": the CSR tier (94%, 87% or 73% silver up to 250% of poverty) with its out-of-pocket maximum and room to the tier line; with a state, whether Medicaid or a Basic Health Program covers that income instead, and the Alaska or Hawaii guideline. Read-only.

coverageYear.description: Marketplace coverage year (2026 or 2027). Defaults to 2026.

state.description: Two-letter state code, if known. Sets Medicaid (expansion states up to 138% FPL), Basic Health Programs (MN, NY, OR, DC up to 200% FPL) and the Alaska and Hawaii poverty guidelines.

magi.description: Household MAGI for the premium tax credit (AGI plus tax-exempt interest and non-taxable Social Security) before any Roth conversion, US dollars a year.

benchmarkMonthly.description: Second-lowest-cost silver plan premium a month for the household, if known; adds the credit in dollars.

tools.name: rmd
tools.description: Answers "what is my RMD this year" and "when do my RMDs start": an IRA owner’s required minimum distribution from last December 31’s balance and birth year (IRS Uniform Lifetime Table, SECURE 2.0 start ages), its due date and the first RMD year. Owner accounts only; a sole-beneficiary spouse more than 10 years younger uses the Joint and Last Survivor table (Table II); inherited IRAs are not covered. Read-only.

year.description: Tax year of the distribution. Defaults to 2026, the latest year with published tables.

priorYearEndBalance.description: Traditional IRA balance on December 31 of the year before, US dollars.

spouseSoleBeneficiary.description: The owner's spouse is the sole designated beneficiary all year. Default false.

spouseBirthYear.description: The spouse's birth year; needed when the spouse is the sole beneficiary.

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: The signed-in Dipperfield account: its email, subscription state, whether the subscriber tools (roth_conversion_path, year_end_check, save_plan) are available, whether save_plan saves straight to the account, and which email reminders it is signed up for. Read-only.

tools.name: roth_conversion_path
tools.description: Answers "how much should I convert to Roth each year to keep my RMDs down" for a subscriber: a year-by-year Roth conversion path from the latest tax year toward a goal (the first RMD at or under an amount, or the traditional balance at an age at or under an amount), either the smallest constant annual conversion that meets it or converting up to a chosen line each year. Each year shows the conversion, RMD, balances and the cost of converting (income tax, IRMAA surcharge two years later, and with a marketplace benchmark the ACA credit given up). Tables are held at the latest published year, amounts in today’s dollars; the real return is the user’s assumption. Read-only.

target.description: The goal: rmd-at-start-age = keep the first required minimum distribution (the year the account owner reaches the RMD start age) at or under maxRmd; balance-at-age = bring the owner’s traditional balance at the end of the year they reach targetAge to or under maxBalance.

targetAge.description: Owner’s age for the balance target (target balance-at-age).

maxBalance.description: Largest acceptable traditional balance at targetAge, in today’s dollars (target balance-at-age), US dollars.

fillToLine.description: Convert each year up to this line instead of the same amount every year. Leave out for the smallest constant annual conversion that meets the target.

acaHouseholdSize.description: Marketplace (ACA) coverage before Medicare: tax household size. With acaBenchmarkMonthly, the premium tax credit a conversion gives up is counted.

acaBenchmarkMonthly.description: Benchmark (second-lowest-cost silver) premium a month for everyone on the plan in 2026, US dollars.

socialSecurityCutPercent.description: Stress scenario the user sets, not a forecast: Social Security pays this percent less from socialSecurityCutFromYear on.

moveToState.description: A move to another state, resident there from moveFromYear on.

tools.name: year_end_check
tools.description: Answers "am I on track this year" and "how much more can I convert before December 31" for a subscriber: this year’s plan (the same inputs as plan_this_year) against what was actually withdrawn, sold and converted so far. Give traditional balances as of the start of the year, or today’s balance plus what was already taken. Returns how tax, AGI and MAGI moved from the plan, the RMD still to take, and engine-computed options for the rest of the year: the plan’s remaining conversion, no more conversion, and converting up to each line, with the added tax of each. Read-only.

tools.name: save_plan
tools.description: Saves a plan_this_year plan (same inputs, plus an optional title) to the signed-in user’s Dipperfield account. It is encrypted before it leaves this server so only the user’s browser can open it, and it joins their saved plans the next time they open them with their passphrase. Needs a Dipperfield subscription. Until the user has saved one plan on dipperfield.com, it returns a link to save the plan there instead. Call it only when the user asks to save. Give each save a requestId and reuse it when retrying that save, so a retry does not save twice.

tools.name: email_reminder_subscribe
tools.description: Signs the signed-in user up for a Dipperfield email reminder, sent to the account’s email. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe. Free for every account. account_status says which reminders the user is already on.

topic.description: year-end: two emails, November 20 and December 15, to run the year-end check and finish Roth conversions before December 31. irmaa-table: one email the day Medicare publishes next year’s IRMAA brackets.

tools.name: email_reminder_unsubscribe
tools.description: Takes the signed-in user off a Dipperfield email reminder. account_status says which reminders the user is on.
